body:
## `browserswipe` event is not available / not dispatched in any browser
### Summary
There is no native `browserswipe` event dispatched on `window` (or any other 
DOM target) in any major browser. Attempting to listen for it silently 
registers a handler that never fires.
```js
window.addEventListener("browserswipe", (event) => {
  if (event.direction === "left" || event.direction === "right") {
    // This callback is never invoked in Chrome, Firefox, Safari, or Edge
  }
});
Steps we attempted to implement swipe-based navigation guarding
Registered window.addEventListener("browserswipe", handler)
The event listener registered without error but the callback was never invoked on any left/right swipe gesture in Chrome, Firefox, Safari, or Edge (desktop and mobile).

Checked event.direction property
Based on available snippets and community references, we expected the event object to carry a direction property ("left" / "right"). Since the event never fired, the property could not be verified.

Searched MDN Web Docs
No documentation exists for a browserswipe event under Window, Document, Element, or any other Web API interface.

Searched the WHATWG HTML Living Standard
No mention of browserswipe exists in the spec.

Searched existing browser vendor documentation
Chromium, WebKit, and Gecko bug trackers and release notes contain no reference to a browserswipe event.

Found only an unmaintained third-party jQuery plugin
The only result named browserSwipe is [kenwheeler/browserSwipe](https://github.com/kenwheeler/browserSwipe) — a jQuery plugin (105 stars, effectively unmaintained) that intercepts trackpad mousewheel delta and does not dispatch a "browserswipe" event on window.

Attempted event.preventDefault() inside the handler
Even if the event had fired, it is unclear whether preventDefault() would suppress the native swipe-to-navigate gesture, since no spec defines the cancellability of such an event.

Fell back to native touch events
We resorted to touchstart / touchend to compute swipe direction manually, as there is no standardised high-level swipe event available.

Request
Please clarify:

Is there any plan to standardise a high-level swipe/gesture event (e.g. swipe, browserswipe, navigationgesture) on window or Navigation that would allow web applications to intercept or observe left/right swipe-to-navigate gestures?
If so, what is the expected event name, target, and event.direction (or equivalent) shape?
Would such an event be cancellable so that apps can prompt users before navigating away (similar to beforeunload)?
A standardised, cancellable swipe-navigation event would fill a real gap — currently there is no reliable way to distinguish a browser back-gesture from programmatic history.go(-1) at the event level.

Environment tested:

Chrome 124+ (desktop & Android)
Safari 17+ (macOS & iOS)
Firefox 125+ (desktop)
Edge 124+ (desktop)
Related:

[Navigation API](https://github.com/WICG/navigation-api)
[beforeunload event](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/window-object.html#unloading-documents)

## Swipe / back navigation — custom handling (summary)

### What we implemented
We added **custom client-side logic** (no CDN gesture library) to:

1. **Distinguish horizontal scrolling from “swipe to leave”**  
   When the user interacts **inside a real horizontal scroll region**, we **do not** intercept: native horizontal scroll (including at the ends) behaves normally.  
   When the gesture is **outside** that context and reads as a strong horizontal swipe / horizontal wheel, we can **block the default** and treat it as a navigation attempt.

2. **Confirm before leaving**  
   In those cases we show a **confirmation dialog** (“moving away from this page”) with **Stay** / **Leave**.  
   **Leave** performs the intended history step (`back` / `forward`) in a controlled way so it doesn’t fight the guard.

3. **Browser Back button**  
   Because we’re on a classic browser router (not the data-router blocking API), we used a **custom history / `popstate` approach**: the first Back is surfaced as the same confirmation flow instead of leaving immediately.

### Technical approach (high level)
- **Non-passive, capture-phase** touch / wheel handling only where needed so `preventDefault` actually applies for document-level gestures.  
- **Heuristics** (distance, horizontal vs vertical dominance) so normal scroll isn’t mistaken for a leave swipe.  
- **Scroll-container detection** so anything that **starts** in horizontal scroll UI stays fully native.

### Caveats
- Some **OS / browser chrome** behaviors may still not be 100% overrideable from the page.

### Outcome
**Swipe-away and Back** can be gated behind **user confirmation**, while **horizontal scrolling in lists/tables** stays unaffected when interaction begins in those areas.
